topic: 佛教起源：一個關於痛苦的問題，如何走過兩千多年
audience: Traditional Chinese general audience; introductory historical and religious literacy
explanation_goal: Explain South Asian origins, traditional life narrative, core teachings and later transmission, preserving uncertainty and the distinction between history and faith.

narrative_route.reason: Chronological historical inquiry is more suitable than a modern life-hack story.
narrative_route.director_review: Spine: inquiry into suffering leads from the ancient Indian context through renunciation and awakening to teachings and historical transmission. The turning point is abandoning self-mortification; end with an open ethical question rather than a promise of cure.
narrative_route.director_plan: Four blocks: context and traditional biography (1-5); search and awakening (6-7); teachings and concrete metaphors (8-11); transmission, evidence/faith distinction and compassion (12-14). Preserve continuous narration and change pages at real sentence boundaries. Each page builds a readable semantic image rather than stock montage.

source_scope.kind: User script preserved in source-script.txt; full established narration retained.
source_scope.limits: Exact dates disputed; four sights and awakening are explicitly framed as Buddhist tradition; images are original illustrative interpretations, not archival evidence.

visual_direction: Complete official8 expressive ink-wash recipe; original South Asian historical subjects, one small vermilion seal; actual anatomy/occlusion masks and aligned contour layers; Waner brush.
subtitle_design: Single burned-in Traditional Chinese layer, 52px conventional Noto Sans CJK, white with thin dark stroke, real WordBoundary timestamps grouped at meaningful pauses. Labels remain above the image, captions below.

beats.text: 今天，當我們想到佛教，可能會想到寺廟、佛像、誦經，或是一句「阿彌陀佛」。但佛教最初出現的地方，並不是中國。它的故事，要回到兩千多年前的南亞，回到一個人對生命的疑問：人為什麼受苦？如果衰老、疾病與死亡無法避免，我們還能怎樣生活？
beats.label: 佛教的起點
beats.visual: An empty mendicant alms bowl beside a worn walking cane and a single fallen leaf; the cane leans naturally against the bowl, separate readable forms. No human figure.

beats.text: 佛教形成於古代印度北部，與恆河流域的思想環境密切相關。創始人是悉達多・喬達摩，也就是後來的釋迦牟尼。關於他的確切生卒年份，學界仍有不同看法，不能把某一組年代當成毫無爭議的答案。比較穩妥的說法，是把故事放在西元前第一千紀中期、古印度思想活躍的時代。
beats.label: 古印度思想
beats.visual: A broad slow river bend in ancient northern India with a single humble riverbank hut and one sparse sal tree, viewed from slightly above; no modern cities, no map labels, no people.

beats.text: 當時，婆羅門傳統重視《吠陀》與祭祀。同時，也有一些離開家庭生活、四處求道的修行者，被稱為沙門。他們探索業、輪迴，以及如何從生命的束縛中解脫。佛陀的探索，就發生在這個思想世界裡。佛教與當時其他傳統既有共同問題，也逐漸提出自己的回答。
beats.label: 沙門與婆羅門
beats.visual: Two visibly separate traditions of seeking: on the left a small ancient Indian brick fire altar with a controlled flame; on the right a wandering ascetic wooden staff and alms bowl. No people or writing.

beats.text: 按照佛教傳統，悉達多出身於釋迦族，出生地是今天尼泊爾境內的藍毗尼。他的成長故事，常被描述為一位受到保護的王子，住在優裕環境中，直到看見外面的世界，才開始思考人生。這裡需要區分：佛陀生平經過長期口傳，後來才寫成經典；熟悉的故事，往往同時包含歷史記憶與宗教敘事。
beats.label: 悉達多的故事
beats.visual: A young South Asian prince Siddhartha in simple ancient north Indian wrapped cotton clothing stands full-body beside an open palace doorway, turning his calm face outward toward the world; a modest carved arch, no crown or halo. Both arms and bare feet clearly visible, limbs separated. Three-quarter frontal view.

beats.text: 其中最著名的，是「四門出遊」。故事說，悉達多先後見到老人、病人、死者，以及一位修行者。這些相遇讓他意識到，財富與地位，也不能讓人永遠年輕、健康，或免於死亡。這段傳統故事，把抽象的生命問題，濃縮成任何人都能理解的畫面：我們珍惜的一切，都可能改變。
beats.label: 四門出遊
beats.visual: Four separate, equally clear small symbolic vignettes across the square: an old walking cane, a simple low sickbed with a pillow, a covered funeral bier with no exposed body, and an ascetic alms bowl beside a walking staff. All four completely separated by empty paper. No people and no gore.

beats.text: 於是，他離開原有生活，開始求道。他向不同老師學習，也嘗試嚴厲的苦行。依照傳統記載，他曾長期節食，讓身體極度虛弱。但他後來放棄這種做法，轉向所謂的「中道」：避開沉溺享樂，也避開折磨身體。中道並不是凡事各退一步，而是尋找真正有助於修行與解脫的方法。
beats.label: 苦行與中道
beats.visual: A lean but healthy South Asian renunciant in a plain wrapped cotton robe walks barefoot along a gentle open path; to the far left is a low table holding a luxury goblet, to the far right is an unused bed of thorns. He follows the open route away from both extremes. Full body, arms separate, no balance scale, no graphic emaciation.

beats.text: 佛教傳統接著說，他在菩提伽耶的一棵菩提樹下禪坐，最終覺悟，成為「佛陀」。佛陀的意思，是覺醒者。釋迦牟尼則有釋迦族聖者的意思。從此，他不只是獨自尋找答案，也開始向別人傳授自己所理解的道路。依照傳統，他在鹿野苑向五位修行者說法，這段故事被視為佛教傳播的重要起點。
beats.label: 菩提樹下
beats.visual: Siddhartha, a South Asian adult with a calm oval face and simple tied dark hair, seated cross-legged in meditation beneath a broad sparse heart-leaf bodhi tree. A simple wrapped cotton monastic robe, hands gently resting separately on the knees, visible head and neck, arms and crossed legs; tree trunk stands to the right behind him without crossing his face. No Chinese architecture, no halo, no written text.

beats.text: 那麼，他究竟教了什麼？最常見的入門概括，是四聖諦：苦、集、滅、道。苦，是正視生命中的不安、失落與不滿足；集，是追問它們如何生起；滅，是指出這些束縛有止息的可能；道，則是實踐的道路。它不是只停留在「人生很苦」，而是從認識問題，走向理解原因，再走向改變。
beats.label: 四聖諦
beats.visual: Four successive symbolic stations of understanding, in a clear left-to-right progression on separate islands of paper: a tangled rope knot, a visible close view of the same knot and its strands, a loosened open loop with separated rope ends, and a clear winding footpath toward a distant open horizon. No arrows or labels in the generated image.

beats.text: 這裡的「苦」，也不表示每一刻都只有痛苦。想像一件讓你開心的事：得到一份工作，遇到喜歡的人，或擁有期待已久的東西。快樂可以是真實的，但條件會變，關係會變，我們自己也會變。這是幫助理解的生活例子：如果執著於「一切必須永遠照我的意思」，變化就可能帶來更多不安。
beats.label: 變化與執著
beats.visual: Close-up of a human hand and short forearm gently gripping a lotus stem; the flower is above the hand, with two petals visibly falling away to the right. The stem is clearly in contact with the fingers, not floating. No head or torso visible. The hand is natural and relaxed, not violent.

beats.text: 佛教也談無常與無我。無常，提醒人注意事物依條件生起，也會改變；無我，涉及對固定、獨立自我的反省。這些都是深刻而複雜的教義，不能只靠一句口號說完。對入門者來說，可以先理解：佛教要求人觀察自己的經驗，看看慾望、憎惡與錯誤理解，如何影響我們的反應。
beats.label: 無常與無我
beats.visual: Three separate phases of the same lotus plant from left to right: a closed bud, an open flower and a drooping seed head. Fine roots touch a shallow pool; a small arc of sun above. No human, no self-help icons, no labels. Clear gaps between the plant phases.

beats.text: 相應的實踐，常以八正道來概括，包括對見解、意向、言語、行為、生計、努力、覺察與專注的訓練。這條道路不只發生在禪坐時，也牽涉日常如何對待他人、如何謀生，以及如何面對自己的心。它有倫理與修習的面向，也有業、輪迴與涅槃等宗教內涵，不能直接等同於現代的放鬆技巧。
beats.label: 八正道
beats.visual: A simple ancient Indian dharma wheel seen straight-on with exactly eight clearly separated spokes, a dark central hub and an unbroken outer rim; below it an open walking path with two subtle footprints, suggesting practical ethical conduct rather than only relaxation. No written words.

beats.text: 隨著弟子與支持者增加，佛教逐漸形成修行共同體。佛陀去世後，教導透過口傳與集體誦習延續，後來形成不同經典傳統。此後的數百年間，佛教持續發展。西元前三世紀，孔雀王朝的阿育王支持佛教，成為其傳播史上的重要人物。但今天各地的佛教樣貌，是長期發展的結果，並非創立之初就全部存在。
beats.label: 僧團與阿育王
beats.visual: An ancient Mauryan stone pillar with a simple lion-shaped capital stands to the left, a modest early Buddhist stupa stands farther right, and a tied bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts lies in the foreground. No legible inscriptions. These are illustrations of different later historical developments, not a claim that written canons existed at the Buddha's first teaching.

beats.text: 回看佛教的起源，我們看見一個南亞思想傳統，如何從對苦與解脫的探索，發展成跨越地域的宗教。王子出走、菩提樹下覺悟，是人們熟悉的傳統敘事；經典如何保存、教義如何演變，則需要歷史研究仔細辨認。理解這兩個層次，既能尊重信仰，也能避免把傳說細節都當成可考證的事實。
beats.label: 歷史與信仰
beats.visual: A carefully opened tied palm-leaf manuscript on the left, its leaves showing only a few nonlegible short lines; on the right a small devotional lotus lamp. They are separate but receive equal visual weight. No modern magnifying glass, no legible pseudo-Sanskrit or Chinese text, no people.

beats.text: 所以，佛教起源的故事，並不只是一座寺廟或一尊佛像的由來。它也保留了一個到今天仍值得思考的問題：當生命不能完全照我們的期待運行時，我們能不能更清楚地理解自己，並學習以不同的方式，面對變化、痛苦，以及他人的處境？
beats.label: 今日的提問
beats.visual: Close-up of two people's forearms and hands: a younger open hand supports an older wrinkled hand from beneath at the center. Gentle, clear physical contact with anatomically readable fingers; neither hand squeezes the other. No faces, no torsos, no jewelry. Empty space surrounds the joined hands.
